ai.literal: Fittingly having investigated, in a manner that [the crime] does not proceed again, proportionately punishing is [the duty of] the king.
ai.translation: A true ruler is one who thoroughly investigates an offense and administers a proportionate punishment, ensuring that the crime is not repeated.
ai.modern: ஒரு குற்றத்தை நடுநிலையோடு ஆராய்ந்து, மீண்டும் அக்குற்றம் நடக்காதவாறு, அதற்குப் பொருத்தமான தண்டனையை வழங்குவதே சிறந்த அரசனின் கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the core principles of justice and deterrence for a ruler. The word 'தக்காங்கு' emphasizes that the investigation must be conducted fittingly and impartially. The phrase 'தலைச்செல்லா வண்ணத்தால்' highlights the goal of deterrence, meaning the punishment should be designed so that the crime does not occur again. Finally, 'ஒத்தாங்கு ஒறுப்பது' demands that the punishment be perfectly proportionate to the gravity of the offense, ensuring justice is neither overly harsh nor weak.

ai.literal: Harshly having raised, gently let strike, long-time prosperity not-leaving those-who-desire.
ai.translation: Let those who desire their prosperity to remain with them for a long time raise the rod of punishment harshly, but strike gently.
ai.modern: தங்களுடைய செல்வம் தங்களை விட்டு நீங்காமல் நீண்ட காலம் நிலைத்திருக்க வேண்டும் என்று விரும்புபவர்கள், தண்டிக்கும்போது கடுமையாகக் கையை ஓங்கி, மெதுவாக அடிக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises rulers on how to administer justice without causing terror. To ensure that their power and prosperity (ஆக்கம்) do not depart (நீங்காமை), they must balance deterrence with mercy. Raising the hand or rod of punishment harshly (கடிதோச்சி) serves as a strong warning to deter wrongdoers, while striking gently (மெல்ல எறிக) ensures the actual punishment is not overly cruel. This balanced approach maintains order while retaining the loyalty and love of the subjects.

ai.literal: If [he] is a cruel-sceptred ruler behaving doing fear-causing [deeds], certainly quickly [he] will be ruined.
ai.translation: If a king rules with a cruel sceptre, performing deeds that cause fear to his subjects, his ruin is certain and will come quickly.
ai.modern: மக்களுக்கு அச்சம் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்து ஆட்சி நடத்தும் கொடுங்கோலனாக ஒரு அரசன் இருந்தால், அவன் நிச்சயம் விரைவில் அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the swift and inevitable downfall of a tyrannical ruler. The term 'வெங்கோலன்' refers to a ruler with a hot or cruel sceptre, symbolizing tyranny. When such a ruler acts in a way that causes fear ('வெருவந்த') among his subjects, his power cannot endure. The poet emphasizes that his destruction is not just possible, but both certain ('ஒருவந்தம்') and rapid ('ஒல்லை'). The key message is that governance through fear and oppression leads directly to a ruler's immediate ruin.

ai.literal: The king who has the painful reputation spoken of him saying 'the ruler is cruel', his lifetime having shortened, will quickly perish.
ai.translation: A king who earns the painful reputation of being called a cruel ruler will find his lifetime shortened and will quickly perish.
ai.modern: நம் அரசன் கொடியவன் என்று மக்களால் பேசப்படும் துன்பகரமான சொல்லைப் பெற்ற அரசன், தன் ஆயுள் காலம் குறைந்து விரைந்து அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns rulers against the dangers of being perceived as tyrannical. When subjects speak of their king as harsh or cruel ('இறைகடியன்'), this painful reputation ('இன்னாச்சொல்') acts as a destructive force. The word 'உறை' in this context refers to the king's span of life or reign. The couplet explains that such a ruler's lifetime is hastened ('கடுகி') to an end, leading to his swift ('ஒல்லை') ruin.

ai.literal: Difficult access and unpleasant face-possessor's great wealth, a ghost having found [wealth], like that, it possesses.
ai.translation: The immense wealth of a ruler who is difficult to access and has a harsh countenance is like wealth found by a ghost—utterly useless to anyone.
ai.modern: காண்பதற்கு அரியவனாய், கடுகடுத்த முகத்தை உடையவனுடைய பெரிய செல்வமானது, பேய் கண்டு பாதுகாப்பதைப் போன்ற தன்மையுடையது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the uselessness of wealth held by an inaccessible and ill-tempered person. The key term 'அருஞ்செவ்வி' refers to someone who is extremely difficult to approach or meet, while 'இன்னா முகத்தான்' describes one who always wears a harsh, unpleasant expression. Their vast fortune ('பெருஞ்செல்வம்') is compared to wealth found or guarded by a ghost ('பேஎய்கண்டு அன்னது'). Just as a ghost cannot enjoy the wealth it hoards and prevents others from using it, the riches of a hostile, unapproachable person benefit absolutely no one.

ai.literal: If a person is of harsh words and without kindness, his great wealth, without enduring, will perish right there.
ai.translation: If a ruler is harsh in speech and devoid of kindness, his vast wealth will perish instantly without enduring.
ai.modern: கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசுபவனாகவும், இரக்கமற்றவனாகவும் ஒருவன் இருந்தால், அவனுடைய பெரிய செல்வம் நிலைத்து நிற்காமல் அப்பொழுதே அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the swift downfall of a leader who lacks basic virtues of speech and empathy. The word 'கண்' (eye) is used here in the sense of kindness or consideration. A ruler who speaks harshly ('கடுஞ்சொல்லன்') and lacks this kind consideration ('கண்ணிலன்') will find that even vast wealth ('நெடுஞ்செல்வம்') cannot save them. Without lasting long ('நீடின்றி'), their power and prosperity will vanish instantly ('ஆங்கே கெடும்') due to the resentment they foster.

ai.literal: Harsh words and limit-exceeded punishment are the file that wears away a king's conquering strength.
ai.translation: Harsh words and excessive punishment are the file that wears away a king's conquering strength.
ai.modern: கடுமையான சொற்களும் எல்லை கடந்த தண்டனையும் ஒரு அரசனுடைய வெல்லும் வலிமையைத் தேய்த்து அழிக்கும் அரம் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns rulers against the dangers of harsh speech and disproportionate punishments. The poet uses the metaphor of an iron file, a tool used to grind down hard objects, to describe these two negative behaviors. Just as a file slowly but surely wears away strong metal, the king's own harsh words and excessive penalties will gradually erode his conquering power and authority. Ultimately, a ruler who terrorizes his subjects with cruelty destroys his own strength from within.

ai.literal: A king who does not deliberate with the guidance of his associates, if he rages with anger guiding him, his wealth will diminish.
ai.translation: The fortune of a king who does not deliberate with the counsel of his ministers, but instead rages and acts out of anger, will surely diminish.
ai.modern: தன் அமைச்சர்களுடன் ஆராய்ந்து செயல்படாத அரசன், கோபத்தின் வழியே சென்று சீறினால், அவனுடைய செல்வம் சுருங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns rulers against acting without counsel and letting anger dictate their behavior. A wise king must deliberate on matters of state with his trusted ministers and associates. If he fails to do so and instead acts impulsively under the influence of anger, he will alienate his supporters and make poor decisions. Consequently, his prosperity and royal fortune will rapidly decline and diminish.

ai.literal: When war has come, a king who has not made defenses, becoming terrified, will swiftly perish.
ai.translation: A king who does not secure his defenses before war arrives will be seized with terror and swiftly perish when the battle comes.
ai.modern: போர் வந்த காலத்தில் தனக்கான அரண் பாதுகாப்பை முன்னரே செய்து கொள்ளாத அரசன், பகைவரைக் கண்டு அஞ்சி, விரைந்து அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the critical need for foresight and defensive preparation in statecraft. The word 'ciṟai' refers to fortifications or protective measures. A ruler who fails to build these defenses before a conflict ('ceru') begins will be caught unprepared. When the enemy finally attacks, the ruler will be overcome with sudden panic ('veruvantu') and meet a swift, inevitable ruin ('veytu keṭum').

ai.literal: A harsh sceptre binds the unlearned; other than that, there is no burden to the earth.
ai.translation: A tyrannical rule surrounds itself only with the ignorant; other than such a reign, there is no greater burden for the earth to bear.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்களைத் தன்பால் சேர்த்துக்கொள்ளும் கொடுங்கோல் ஆட்சி; அதைத் தவிர இந்த பூமிக்கு வேறு பெரிய சுமை எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the heavy burden of tyranny on the world. A cruel ruler with a harsh sceptre (கடுங்கோல்) naturally attracts and binds (பிணிக்கும்) only ignorant, unlearned people (கல்லார்) to his administration, as wise people avoid him. The poet asserts that there is no greater burden (பொறை) weighing down the earth (நிலக்கு) than this combination of a tyrant and his foolish counselors.
